api_key.instructions: Open fal’s dashboard keys page, create a key, and copy it. The key has the form `key_id:key_secret` and is sent as an `Authorization: Key` header. Verification reads the API’s own published contract and runs no model.
api_key.notes: Key scheme with the combined id:secret credential; one bounded read-only GET of the published API contract. No model runs, writes or token minting.

api_key.instructions: Create an API credential in the Higgsfield Console and copy the key ID and secret. Paste them here joined with a colon (`key_id:key_secret`); they travel as an `Authorization: Key` header and only list the models your account can reach.
api_key.notes: Key scheme with the combined id:secret credential; one bounded read-only POST listing the account’s models. No generation submissions.

api_key.instructions: Supply your Linq Partner messaging Bearer token. Test and Save read the sending phone numbers assigned to your partner. Use List messaging lines to read the current phone numbers, line types and reputations. This is the iMessage/RCS/SMS Partner API, not the separate WhatsApp API or a business-card account. No messages are sent.
api_key.notes: Official OpenAPI BearerAuth; fixed GET /api/partner/v3/phone_numbers, no request body or invented query. Strict line inventory must validate before a saved verification proof. No message writes, webhook setup, token minting or refresh.

api_key.instructions: Supply a **platform access token** minted from your own client credentials using the [official access-token endpoint](https://docs.agentcard.sh/api-reference/access-tokens/create). It expires after one hour; replace it when authorization expires. Do not enter a user connection token or a member-card token. The same HTTPS host serves test and production; the token decides the mode. This connection only reads your platform organization and mode, never cards, card credentials or payment writes. Both token minting and renewal remain explicit in your own Agentcard account.
api_key.notes: Platform Bearer only; fixed GET /api/v2 with api_v2, organization_id and test_mode required. No member/card endpoints, token minting, refresh or environment fallback.

api_key.instructions: Install the **Local REST API** community plugin in Obsidian, copy its API key, and enter the HTTPS endpoint it serves (default `127.0.0.1:27124`). Trust the plugin’s certificate authority in this browser (download it from the plugin at `https://127.0.0.1:27124/obsidian-local-rest-api.crt`) so the connection can open. Verification reads the plugin’s own status document; your notes are never read here.
api_key.notes: Bearer key against the plugin’s local HTTPS endpoint on the machine’s loopback; one bounded read-only status call whose authenticated flag must be true. No note reads, writes or events.

api_key.instructions: Sign in to the [Amazon Nova developer console](https://nova.amazon.com/dev/api), generate an API key and copy it. The [Nova developer documentation](https://nova.amazon.com/dev/documentation) says the API takes the key as a Bearer token. Without an Origin header on 2026-10-12: POST with a fake Bearer key answers 403 with an empty body (CloudFront/Amazon authorizer); POST with no Authorization header answers 500 with an HTML error page (not 401/403, but the app always sends a key). Rejected GETs: /v1/models, /v1/models/{id}, /v1/files, /v1/account all answer the same empty 403 for any Bearer-shaped fake, and so does GET /v1/zzz-nonexistent, so the 403 comes from the authorizer before routing and says nothing about whether the route exists; no Amazon page documents a models, account or usage route (the first-party docs page is a client-rendered app that returns no text, and LiteLLM lists only chat completions and responses). A valid-key answer was not exercised. key_url /dev/api is the site's own route for key generation (the app bundle's BUILDER_STUDIO_DEV_APIS route renders the 'generate API key' component), not a page that could be fetched here.

api_key.notes: GET /v1/models on api.inference.crusoecloud.com, the OpenAI-compatible Serverless Inference host. Read-only, bills nothing. Without an Origin header on 2026-10-12: a fake Bearer answers 401 {"errors":["Authentication failed"],"id":"..."} and no key answers 401 {"errors":["Authentication failed"]}. Route-specific: GET /v1/zzz-nonexistent and /v1/files with the fake key answer 404 on this host, so /v1/models is a real authenticated route (the docs describe the host as OpenAI-API compatible and use the OpenAI SDK against /v1, but print no curl for /v1/models, hence medium). Origin sensitivity worth knowing for the extension: with an Origin of chrome-extension://<32 letters> plus the fake key the host answers the same 401 and echoes that origin in access-control-allow-origin; with Origin https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io plus a key it answers an empty 403 from the edge (the earlier batch saw this), so the verify call must be sent from the extension, not the page. Documented alternates live on a different host: GET https://api.intelligence.crusoecloud.com/v1/fine_tuning/jobs?limit=20 and /v1/files (Serverless Fine-Tuning docs; fake key 401 {"detail":"Authentication failed"}, no key 403 Cloudflare HTML), rejected because that host is not in the catalog row's egress authorities. Caveats: (1) the host differs from the catalog's gateway host; (2) Helicone documents a separate EU host (eu.api.helicone.ai) and a US-host request with an EU-region key is expected to be refused (eu.api.helicone.ai also answers 401 to a fake key; not testable without a key); (3) the docs do not say which key type or permission the route needs. Z.AI's published API reference and quick start do not list a GET /models route (they document chat, image, video, audio and tool routes only); it is the OpenAI-compatible route and it demands a credential. Authenticated access was not exercised, so a 2xx for a valid key (including a GLM Coding Plan key, which the docs say uses a separate endpoint) is unproven. Chat road warning: the preflight for POST /api/paas/v4/chat/completions (and /api/coding/paas/v4/chat/completions) answers 200 with no access-control-allow-origin, so a browser blocks inference calls from the page (PreflightMissingAllowOriginHeader in Chromium) even though this key check works.

api_key.instructions: Open the [Zhipu AI documentation](https://docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing), create an API key in its console and copy it.
api_key.notes: Models list answered an unauthenticated request with an auth refusal, so the route needs a credential; preflight for GET (authorization) and POST (authorization, content-type) from the audited origin admitted it on 2026-10-11. Authenticated access was not exercised.

api_key.instructions: Enter your Key ID in Razorpay API key and your Key Secret below. Both credentials are sealed in this vault. Test and live keys use the same endpoint. This connection only reads the first 20 payment summaries; it cannot capture payments, create refunds or change payment data.

Create a scoped Bitbucket API token with read:user:bitbucket and read:repository:bitbucket. Add write:repository:bitbucket for encrypted vault backups. Paste the API token here; it is sealed in this vault. For backups, optionally supply all three repository fields and an existing branch. Browser requests use your approved native HTTPS route when configured. No OAuth app or app password is used by this method.
Open Asana's developer console, create a **Personal access token**, and copy it. The token is sent as a Bearer token to the v1.0 API.
api_key.notes: Bearer PAT; one bounded read-only identity call. No writes, token minting or refresh.

api_key.instructions: Create an Azure Resource Manager access token with `az account get-access-token --scope https://management.azure.com/.default` and paste it here. Verification lists subscriptions with one bounded read-only request; the token is sealed on this device and can be replaced when it expires.
api_key.notes: Azure Resource Manager Bearer token; one bounded read-only subscription listing.
